 Take a campaign's audience from targeting to deployment. Turn the written criteria for a campaign or program into an audience list from BDC's client and prospect data, applying the eligibility and consent rules. Our partnerships with industry leaders like Palantir, NVIDIA, and OpenAI underscore our commitment to excellence.  Unit8 is dedicated to driving AI adoption in non-digital industries and accelerating their digital transformation. We invest in projects that matter, including pro-bono initiatives and “engineering for good” causes.
 The opportunity
 Following our growth in Europe and our recent expansion into the US market in early 2026, Unit8 is taking its next strategic step in North America. We are looking for a commercially minded Head of Legal to help establish our Canadian presence in Montréal and to be the senior legal voice for our North American business.
 This is, above all, a business-enabling role. You are the person who sits with our sales, delivery and finance teams, understands what a deal needs to succeed, and turns complex legal risk into clear, practical positions that help us close. You are the bridge between our clients’ legal and procurement teams and our own business, fluent enough in both to protect Unit8 without slowing it down.
 You own the contracting and legal strategy for Canada and the US. You negotiate our client and purchasing agreements, decide what is handled in-house and what goes to external counsel, and build a modern, AI-enabled contract review process. Reporting directly to our CFO, you also lead our junior In-house Legal Counsel in Europe and act as the escalation point for contract reviews across our other geographies.
 As one of our first Canadian hires, you will help shape how Unit8 contracts in North America, which standards and playbooks we work from, and how our legal function scales as we grow.
 What you'll do
 As our Head of Legal, you will be the senior legal voice for Unit8 in North America. Based in our Montreal office and reporting directly to our CFO in Europe, you will own commercial, procurement and governance legal work for our Canadian and US business, and lead a small, global legal function. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you’ll close deals, shape how we contract, and build a modern, AI-enabled legal process from the ground up.
 Close the deals that grow our North American business 
 Review, draft and negotiate client contracts: MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, data processing agreements, IP and licensing terms, subcontracting and partnership agreements, as well as purchasing contracts.
 Lead face-to-face and remote negotiations with client legal and procurement teams, preparing the negotiation strategy, fallback positions and risk assessment for every material deal.
 Advise our sales, delivery and finance teams on liability caps, indemnities, IP ownership and data protection, in plain language they can act on.
 Own our Canadian and US contract templates, playbooks and standard positions: learn them quickly, improve them where needed, and use them to build client proposals and contracts.
 Work alongside our DPO and CISO on data protection topics.
 Keep our North American entities in good shape 
 Prepare and maintain corporate governance documents for our Canadian and US entities.
 Support the CFO and the board on corporate structure matters.
 Decide what stays in-house and what goes out 
 Route matters to external counsel in Canada, the US or Europe when it makes sense, weighing urgency, complexity and cost.
 Select, brief and manage external counsel, own the external legal budget and review invoices against scope.
 Lead and grow the legal team 
 Manage and coach our junior In-house Legal Counsel based in Europe : set priorities, allocate work and review output across time zones.
 Act as backup reviewer for EU and MEA contracts when our European counsel is at capacity.
 Report to the CFO on workload, open matters, material contractual risks and external legal spend.
 Build an AI-enabled legal function 
 Run and continuously improve our end-to-end contract review process: intake, triage, turnaround targets, approval thresholds and sign-off.
 Govern and develop AI tools for first-pass review, clause comparison and redlining, with clear rules on confidentiality, human sign-off and quality control. You’ll be working at an AI company, so expect to put these tools to real use.
 Track review volumes and turnaround times and use the data to make the process faster and better.
 To be clear on scope: employment and labour law, as well as litigation and dispute resolution, are not part of this role and remain with HR and external counsel.
 Who you are
 You hold a law degree and are a member in good standing of the Barreau du Québec (or another Canadian law society with eligibility to practise in Quebec).
 You bring 7–10 years of experience as legal counsel in commercial and corporate law, in-house or at a law firm or legal service provider.
 You have negotiated services agreements, SOWs and software terms in an IT, SaaS or professional services company.
 You’re confident with Quebec civil law and the common-law framework of the other provinces, particularly Ontario.
 You have a working knowledge of US commercial contract law: you can work from our US templates, spot issues and know when to bring in US counsel. (You won’t be practising US law.)
 You’re familiar with Quebec Law 25, PIPEDA and, at a basic level, US state privacy laws.
 You have managed at least one direct report or a small team, and you enjoy developing people.
 You’re fully bilingual in French and English, and comfortable negotiating and drafting in both languages.
 You have built or redesigned a legal intake and review process, and you measure turnaround and quality.
 You read contracts for their business impact on margin, cash and delivery risk, not only for legal exposure.
 You’re curious about AI in legal work: you use these tools, understand their limits, and know how to govern them responsibly.
 You thrive working autonomously as the only lawyer in your region, while staying closely connected to a team in Europe.
 Language

 Real impact: your work directly enables projects that bring AI and data science to some of the largest companies in traditional industries.
 A modern legal function where AI tools are part of the daily workflow, not an afterthought.
 Flexible working: 30–40 hours per week to be agreed with you, with at least 2–3 days per week in our Montreal office and the rest remote. Your day starts by 8:00 or 9:00 AM Eastern to overlap with our European colleagues.

 A collaborative, international team of 150+ engineers, data scientists and consultants who care about doing great work, including pro-bono and “engineering for good” projects.

 Calendar and priorities

ABOUT JOBBER

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber, they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.



The Team

Analytics sits within Jobber’s Strategy & Analytics department, Jobber’s internal consulting team and decision-support mechanism that connects data and business insight with the rest of the organization. Analytics is a central function that exists to drive business outcomes across Jobber’s ecosystem.



The Role

Jobber is looking for a Manager, Customer Analytics (Sales & Marketing) to lead the analytics function supporting our Marketing & Channels and Sales & Partnerships pods. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Customer Analytics, this leader will manage a team of analysts and partner closely with Directors, Senior Directors, and VPs across Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Sales, Partnerships, MarketingOps, SalesOps, and Finance.

In this role, you will set the technical, methodological, and strategic direction for high-impact Sales and Marketing analytics. You will own the measurement infrastructure that helps Jobber connect acquisition investment to subscription revenue growth, understand marketing effectiveness, evaluate channel and partnership performance, and improve visibility into CAC, LTV, payback, sales efficiency, revenue funnel performance, and go-to-market ROI.

This role requires a leader who combines strong people leadership, hands-on technical depth, and deep Sales and Marketing domain expertise. You will build trusted relationships with senior leaders, raise the bar for analytical quality, and develop analysts who can translate rigorous measurement into better growth decisions.

You will also help Jobber advance Analytics 2.0 in practice by using self-serve analytics, automation, responsible AI, and agentic workflows to scale trusted decision support and create more capacity for strategic, high-judgment analytical work.



 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Team Leadership & Analytics Operating Model

 - Hire, onboard, lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of analysts supporting Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Sales, and Partnerships, setting clear expectations and building the team’s capabilities as Jobber’s Sales and Marketing analytics needs scale.

 - Establish a clear engagement and prioritization model for Sales and Marketing Analytics, creating scalable operating rhythms that balance strategic analysis, recurring reporting, cross-functional initiatives, self-serve enablement, and ad hoc stakeholder needs.

 - Build a culture of analytical excellence, high accountability, curiosity, strong QA, documentation, peer review, business ownership, and continuous improvement.

 - Partner with Analytics Engineering, BI, Data Science, Data Engineering, MarketingOps, and SalesOps to strengthen the data foundation, metric definitions, reporting infrastructure, and governed datasets that support Sales and Marketing decision-making.

Sales & Marketing Analytics Strategy

 - Lead the analytics roadmap across Jobber’s Marketing & Channels and Sales & Partnerships pods, ensuring the team is focused on the highest-impact opportunities across customer acquisition, demand generation, sales productivity, channel performance, partnership growth, and revenue efficiency.

 - Partner with Sales and Marketing leadership to define success metrics, identify growth opportunities, evaluate strategic bets, and translate ambiguous business questions into clear analytical approaches and actionable recommendations.

 - Help Jobber understand not just what is happening across the go-to-market funnel, but why it is happening, what it means, and what leaders should do next.

Performance Marketing, Demand Generation & Channel Measurement

 - Define and evolve Jobber’s marketing measurement framework across Marketing Mix Modelling (MMM), Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA), incrementality, experimentation, and forecasting, ensuring these methods work together as a unified system for decision-making rather than as siloed tools.

 - Lead the design and operationalization of advanced marketing measurement approaches, including MMM, MTA, incrementality testing, spend efficiency curves, saturation analysis, and diminishing returns modelling, connecting marketing and channel investment to subscription revenue, CAC, payback, LTV, pipeline quality, and long-term customer value.

 - Set standards for how analysts select, build, quality-assure, and interpret advanced measurement methods, including when to use MMM, MTA, incrementality testing, causal inference, forecasting, or simpler diagnostic approaches.

 - Partner with Performance Marketing, Demand Generation, Brand Marketing & Communications, Partnerships, Finance, and MarketingOps to evaluate spend efficiency, channel mix, conversion quality, saturation, diminishing returns, and budget allocation trade-offs, including scenario analysis ahead of planning cycles.

Sales, Partnerships & Revenue Funnel Analytics

 - Lead analytics that help Sales and Partnerships leaders understand funnel health, lead quality, conversion performance, rep and team productivity, pipeline creation, sales-assisted revenue, partner/referral performance, and opportunities to improve go-to-market efficiency.

 - Build frameworks, dashboards, models, and decision-support tools that help leaders monitor performance, diagnose issues, and make better planning, resourcing, and prioritization decisions.

 - Connect sales and marketing performance into a unified view of acquisition economics, helping Jobber understand how demand, channel mix, sales motion, and customer quality translate into durable revenue growth.

Executive Influence & Storytelling

 - Bring an analytical perspective to growth strategy, planning, investment decisions, and operating reviews with Directors, Senior Directors, VPs, and cross-functional leaders.

 - Translate complex analytical work into clear narratives, trade-offs, and recommendations that senior leaders can act on.

Analytics 2.0 & AI-Powered Decision Support

 - Contribute to Jobber’s Analytics 2.0 roadmap by identifying where AI, ML, automation, and agentic analytics can accelerate Sales and Marketing measurement, forecasting, diagnostics, storytelling, and self-serve decision support.

 - Partner with Analytics Engineering, BI, Data Science, and Data Engineering to operationalize AI-assisted workflows and analytics agents for anomaly detection, campaign diagnostics, forecasting, attribution, causal inference, narrative generation, documentation, and QA.

 - Champion governed self-serve analytics and trusted metrics so Sales and Marketing leaders can answer recurring performance questions without routing every request through an analyst, while preserving analytical quality and clear ownership.

 - Help analysts adopt AI responsibly, validating outputs, understanding limitations, documenting methods, and using automation to create more capacity for strategic modelling and business influence.

 


WHAT YOU BRING

Sales & Marketing Analytics Expertise

 - Deep experience in Sales, Marketing, Growth, Revenue, Demand Generation, Performance Marketing, Channels, Partnerships, or GTM analytics, ideally in a high-growth SaaS or subscription business.

 - Strong understanding of customer acquisition economics, including CAC, LTV, payback period, funnel conversion, pipeline quality, channel performance, sales efficiency, partner/referral performance, and subscription revenue growth.

 - Deep, hands-on experience with marketing and GTM measurement approaches, including attribution, incrementality testing, experimentation, forecasting, budget allocation, and the practical limitations of each method.

 - Experience helping senior Sales and Marketing leaders define success metrics, evaluate performance, diagnose growth opportunities, and make better decisions across the go-to-market funnel.

 - Familiarity with marketing, sales, CRM, ad platform, lifecycle, partnerships, and revenue funnel data, including paid search, paid social, organic, referral, brand, partnerships, lifecycle marketing, and platform-specific measurement constraints from tools such as Google Ads, Meta, and programmatic ad platforms.

 - Hands-on experience building or significantly contributing to advanced marketing measurement approaches such as Marketing Mix Modelling, Multi-Touch Attribution, incrementality experiments, geo or matched-market tests, synthetic control, spend efficiency curves, or causal inference methods, with the judgment to evaluate, challenge, and improve vendor or platform-reported outputs.

Technical & Methodological Skills

 - Expert-level SQL skills, with the ability to work across complex data structures, build analytical datasets, and review analytical logic with confidence.

 - Strong hands-on analytical skills, including performance measurement, exploratory analysis, cohort analysis, impact evaluation, experimentation, forecasting, scenario analysis, segmentation, predictive modelling, and causal inference techniques such as difference-in-differences, synthetic control, propensity score matching, or regression discontinuity.

 - Strong proficiency in Python or R for modelling, automation, statistical analysis, and productionized analytics workflows; experience with MMM libraries or statistical modelling frameworks such as Robyn, Meridian, PyMC-Marketing, Bayesian modelling frameworks, or equivalent tools is a strong asset.

 - Strong statistical judgment, including comfort with confidence intervals, effect size estimation, variance, seasonality, bias, model uncertainty, and balancing analytical rigour with pragmatic business decision-making.

 - Experience with modern data stacks and BI tools such as dbt, Snowflake, Redshift, Looker, Tableau, or similar platforms, with a strong ability to build scalable, trusted reporting and decision-support assets.

Business & Leadership Skills

 - Proven experience as a people leader in analytics, with a strong track record of developing, coaching, and empowering high-performing analysts.

 - Strong strategic judgment, with the ability to shape priorities, influence senior leaders, and connect analytical work to company-level growth outcomes.

 - Experience owning an analytics roadmap in a fast-moving environment with competing stakeholder needs and high-impact business decisions.

 - Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build trust, clarify ambiguous asks, manage trade-offs, and influence Directors, Senior Directors, VPs, and cross-functional leaders through data-backed recommendations.

 - Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis, uncertainty, and trade-offs into clear executive-ready narratives.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead AI-assisted analytics adoption across a team, including identifying high-value use cases, setting QA and governance expectations, validating outputs, improving documentation, accelerating analysis, and helping analysts use AI to deliver better decision support without compromising quality.

 


WHO YOU ARE

 - You are a strategic analytics leader who can operate at multiple altitudes. You can zoom into technical details when needed, but you always connect the work back to business decisions and outcomes.

 - You are a strong people leader who creates clarity, raises the bar, and helps analysts do the best work of their careers.

 - You are proactive and resourceful. You do not wait to be handed perfectly formed questions; you identify the highest-value problems, frame the trade-offs, and guide stakeholders toward better decisions.

 - You are deeply curious about Sales and Marketing performance. You want to understand what drives acquisition, conversion, channel effectiveness, sales efficiency, partnership growth, and long-term customer value.

 - You hold a high bar for analytical quality and measurement rigour, while staying pragmatic about what is useful, deployable, and decision-relevant in a real business environment.

 - You communicate with clarity and confidence, especially when explaining uncertainty, trade-offs, and imperfect evidence to senior stakeholders.

 - You are comfortable making trade-offs visible. You know how to say yes to the highest-impact work while helping stakeholders understand what must be deprioritized.

 - You are excited by Analytics 2.0. You see emerging tools and operating models as ways to redesign how analytics teams deliver trusted, scalable decision support, not just as productivity shortcuts.

Compensation

We’re Hiring! Join By Lawyers as a Canadian Legal Content Editor 
 At By Lawyers, we create practical, trusted legal resources that help lawyers work more efficiently and confidently. We’re looking for a knowledgeable and detail-oriented legal professional to develop and maintain our Canadian practice guides, with a focus on Ontario, British Columbia and Alberta.
 In this role, you’ll combine legal research, editorial writing and practical legal expertise to keep our content current, develop new guides from the ground up, and turn complex legal developments into clear, actionable guidance for practitioners. You’ll also engage with lawyers and law firms to demonstrate our products, respond to feedback and help shape the resources they rely on every day.
 Working closely with our publication and quality teams, as well as colleagues in Canada, Australia, the UK and New Zealand, you’ll play an important role in delivering high-quality legal content that makes a real difference to legal practice.
 By Lawyers exclusively integrates with LEAP Legal Software. As such, you will be working closely with various LEAP Canada teams.
 About By Lawyers 
 By Lawyers publishes practical legal guides for lawyers in Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom and New Zealand. Each guide pairs a commentary written for practitioners with a full suite of precedents, delivered through a matter plan. Our content is written by lawyers, for lawyers.
 Our Canadian guides cover Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta across real estate, family law, wills and estates, civil litigation, corporate law, and practice management, with the list growing. We are looking for a lawyer to take ownership of that content. A law clerk or paralegal with extensive experience will also be considered. This posting is based in our Toronto office for a new role being added to the Canadian team.
 ***Note this By Lawyers role will work out of our affiliated downtown Toronto office managed by LEAP Legal Software (Canada) Limited and the Canadian payroll and employment benefits will be managed by LEAP on behalf of By Lawyers. We work on a hybrid work model that requires a minimum of 3 days a week in office. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 As a Legal Editor, you are responsible for the accuracy, currency and usability of By Lawyers guides. Key responsibilities include but are not limited to:
 Keep the Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta guides current by monitoring legislative amendments, new case law, practice directions and form changes, and revising commentaries, precedents and matter plans as needed.
 Write new guides from the ground up: scope the matter type, draft the commentary and the precedent suite, and build the matter plan for publication.
 Research points of law and practice across our Canadian jurisdictions and turn them into clear, practical guidance that a busy practitioner can act on.
 Work to the By Lawyers house style and editorial process and take your work through review and publication with our publication and quality teams.
 Demonstrate By Lawyers products to lawyers and law firms, online and in person, as a credible subject matter expert.
 Respond to client questions and feedback.
 Collaborate with colleagues in Canada, Australia, the UK and New Zealand.
 LL.B. or J.D. degree with active membership in good standing with a Canadian Law Society; Called to the Bar in Ontario or another Canadian common law jurisdiction; we will also consider experienced, licensed paralegals or law clerks in Ontario for this role 
 Minimum of 3 years’ experience as a practising lawyer, OR 7 years' as a paralegal or law clerk, in one or more practice areas
 Must be currently legally eligible to work in Canada without sponsorship
 Excellent written and verbal English communication skills with the ability to write for practitioners rather than for a court or a client
 Strong organizational and project management abilities with a focus on quality and detail
 Strong legal research and analytical skills with good judgment to know when a source settles a question and when it does not
 Strong presentation skills
 Proficiency with Microsoft Word (including styles, tracked changes and comments) and Outlook 
 Attention to detail and the discipline to work steadily through a large volume of content without losing accuracy
 Independent, proactive and curious
 Highly accountable to effectively manage your own workload and meet publication deadlines
 A Strong Asset, but Not Required: 
 Experience working in more than one of Ontario, British Columbia and Alberta jurisdictions
 Experience with or working knowledge of workflow tools e.g. Trello and Confluence
 Legal publishing, precedent drafting or knowledge management experience
 Familiarity with LEAP or other legal practice management software
 Comfortable using AI tools in a professional workflow
 Application Requirements: 
 Current resume
 A brief covering letter, no more than one page, on your practice background and why legal publishing appeals to you
 A writing sample of 500 to 1,000 words that explains a point of law or procedure to a practitioner. Something you have written for work is fine, with all client details removed.
 Why this role 
 Your work is read and relied on every day by lawyers across Canada
 Broad exposure across areas of law and three provinces. You will learn more law here than in a single practice group
 The skills of a practising lawyer without the billable hour, court deadlines or client files
 A small, collegial team with real ownership of your portfolio
 Work/life balance – while there may be times that extended hours are required during peak period or projects, this is generally a ‘9-5’ role.
 Why work at LEAP? 
 There are endless opportunities within our business to progress and grow your career and full training is provided so an aptitude and hunger to learn is essential. We offer:
 Competitive compensation with a base salary. The base salary band for this role ranges from: $80,000 CAD - $100,000 CAD annually. Salary will be based on level of experience.
 Excellent group insurance benefits
 RRSP with employer matching

 Hybrid working model at our beautiful and modern downtown Toronto office as well as work from home days
 Collaborative and inclusive work environment filled with learning and support

 An overview of this role 
 As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.
 Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.
 What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.

That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.

 Technical Ownership  
 Own technical solutions end-to-end, translating customer and business needs into scalable, production-ready software. 
 Design, develop, test, deploy, and support software throughout its lifecycle. 
 Take accountability for solution quality, maintainability, security, scalability, and operational excellence.

 Drive technical execution while balancing delivery speed with engineering quality. 
 Proactively identify risks, remove blockers, and continuously improve engineering effectiveness. 
 Software Engineering  
 Design and build scalable backend services, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. 
 Develop modern full-stack applications across backend and frontend technologies. 
 Write clean, maintainable, well-tested, and secure code. 
 Optimize application performance, scalability, observability, and reliability. 
 Contribute to architecture, technical design, and platform evolution. 
 Improve developer experience through automation, tooling, and reusable engineering patterns. 
 AI Engineering  
 Design and build AI-powered product capabilities that create measurable customer value. 
 Develop AI agents, agentic workflows, and intelligent automation solutions. 
 Integrate Large Language Models (LLMs), AI services, and external APIs into production applications.

 Partner closely with Product Managers and Designers to understand customer problems and business objectives. 
 Translate customer needs into scalable, high-quality software solutions that deliver measurable business value. 
 Participate in technical discovery, solution design, estimation, and delivery planning. 
 Build solutions that prioritize accessibility, usability, reliability, and customer outcomes. 
 Engineering Excellence

 Participate in peer code reviews and architectural design reviews. 
 Improve engineering standards through documentation, automation, and continuous improvement. 
 Participate in production support, incident response, root cause analysis, and operational improvements.

 Mentor engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and knowledge sharing. 
 Influence technical direction through collaboration and sound engineering judgment. 
 Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

 Strong full-stack development experience.

 Strong experience with cloud platforms (AWS preferred).

 AI agent and agentic workflow development. 
 Large Language Model (LLM) integrations. 
 Prompt engineering and prompt optimization. 
 Tool calling and AI orchestration. 
 AI evaluation and testing. 
 Rapid prototyping using AI technologies. 
 AI-assisted software development.

 Technical Skills

 TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, or C# 
 React or modern frontend frameworks 
 Node.js and backend application frameworks 
 REST APIs and GraphQL 
 AWS cloud services 
 Docker and Kubernetes 
 MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis 
 GitHub Actions or CI/CD platforms 
 Infrastructure as Code 
 Observability and monitoring platforms 
 Event-driven architectures 
 Serverless computing 
 Leadership Competencies  
 Demonstrated leadership competencies , including: 
 Take ownership and accountability for outcomes. 
 Deliver with urgency while maintaining high engineering standards. 
 Make informed technical decisions independently. 
 Adapt quickly to changing priorities and business needs. 
 Solve complex problems with a pragmatic, customer-focused mindset. 
 Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 Mentor others and contribute to a high-performing engineering culture. 
 Continuously learn and embrace emerging technologies, particularly AI. 
 What Success Looks Like

 Independently deliver complex software solutions from design through production. 
 Build AI-powered capabilities that improve customer outcomes and engineering productivity. 
 Contribute to the evolution of Fable's platform architecture and engineering standards. 
 Improve software quality, reliability, scalability, and operational excellence. 
 Accelerate engineering execution through AI-assisted development and automation. 
 Be recognized as a trusted technical leader who consistently delivers high-impact outcomes. 
 Our values  
 To lead, listen first  
You amplify voices that are less often heard and create space for those voices to grow. The quality of an idea doesn't correlate with the loudness of someone's voice. 
 The brain is a muscle  
If you're going to do something, you will do it well. Practice often and rest when needed. Give your mind what it needs to thrive. 
 Unlearn to learn  
What did we learn growing up, and what do we need to unlearn? It's essential to understanding our personal bias and position so that we can grow.

AquaEye is a fast-growing technology company transforming the global water rescue industry through rapid-deployment intelligent sonar solutions. Our flagship product, AquaEye, is a handheld sonar device designed to help first responders locate drowning victims faster and more effectively.
 As we continue to advance AquaEye's detection capabilities and develop new products, we are looking for a hands-on Applied Scientist with deep experience working with complex real-world sensor data, signal processing, acoustics, sound engineering, sonar, or related scientific data.
 This role sits at the intersection of signal processing, data science, machine learning and embedded product development.
 We are particularly interested in someone fascinated by the data underneath the algorithm: understanding what our sonar signals contain, identifying and extracting meaningful information from noisy real-world data, determining which features matter, and using that understanding to develop effective detection methodologies and machine learning solutions.
 You do not need to come from the water-rescue industry or have worked specifically with AquaEye's technology. Experience interpreting complex signals in fields such as sonar, acoustics, audio/sound engineering, radar, medical devices, telecommunications, geophysics, remote sensing, robotics, industrial sensing or other sensor-based systems may be highly transferable.
 This is a highly hands-on role within a small, collaborative product-development team. You will work closely with hardware, embedded software, engineering and product leadership to help determine the next generation of AquaEye's core detection technology.
 Job Responsibilities:
 Signal Processing & Applied Data Science
 Lead the exploration and interpretation of raw sonar and sensor data to understand the information contained within the signal.
 Design, evaluate and improve signal-processing methodologies used to extract meaningful features from complex and noisy real-world data.
 Investigate signal characteristics across different environments and operating conditions to understand sources of noise, variability and performance degradation.
 Apply techniques such as filtering, spectral analysis, time- and frequency-domain analysis, feature extraction and Fourier transforms, where appropriate.
 Determine which characteristics of the underlying data are most useful for detection and classification.
 Develop experimental approaches to distinguish meaningful signal from environmental noise and other confounding factors.
 Work closely with hardware and embedded engineering teams to understand how sensor design, device configuration and operating conditions influence data quality.
 Machine Learning & Algorithm Development
 Design and develop detection methodologies using the most appropriate combination of signal processing, statistical methods, machine learning and algorithmic approaches.
 Develop, train, validate and deploy machine learning models where ML provides meaningful value.
 Evaluate both simple and complex approaches rather than assuming a particular ML architecture is the answer.
 Convert scientific and algorithmic concepts into production-quality code for embedded and/or cloud environments.
 Define meaningful performance metrics, with particular attention to false positives, false negatives, generalization and performance across different operating environments.
 Continually experiment with and evaluate new approaches to improve detection performance.
 Optimize algorithms and models for performance within embedded hardware constraints.
 Data Strategy & Field Experimentation
 Help define what data AquaEye needs to collect to improve its detection capabilities.
 Design experiments and field-data collection initiatives that test specific hypotheses and address gaps within existing datasets.
 Establish methodologies for data cleaning, preprocessing, labelling, quality assurance and validation.
 Identify biases, gaps and underrepresented operating conditions within existing datasets.
 Build datasets that represent the range of real-world environments in which AquaEye is deployed.
 Develop rigorous approaches for evaluating whether improvements observed during development generalize to real-world field conditions.
 Product Development & Technical Direction
 Work alongside Product, Hardware, Embedded Software and executive leadership to define the technical roadmap for AquaEye's detection capabilities.
 Translate scientific findings into practical product improvements.
 Help determine when challenges should be addressed through better data, signal processing, algorithm development, machine learning, hardware changes, or a combination of approaches.
 Participate in field testing, customer trials and product validation.
 Communicate complex scientific and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
 Contribute to the longer-term development of AquaEye's data science and machine learning capabilities.
 Technical Leadership & Team Development
 Serve as a senior technical resource within the product-development team.
 Provide technical guidance and mentorship as AquaEye's data science and ML capabilities grow.
 Establish rigorous scientific and engineering practices around experimentation, validation, documentation and reproducibility.
 Conduct technical reviews and encourage knowledge sharing across engineering disciplines.
 Help define the skills and capabilities required as the future data science/ML team expands.
 Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, Acoustics, Signal Processing, Data Science, or another relevant quantitative discipline.

 Demonstrated experience working directly with raw signals, sensor data or other complex physical-world datasets.
 Strong understanding of signal processing and/or time-series data analysis.
 Experience investigating noisy real-world data and identifying meaningful features, patterns and sources of variability.

The Project Coordinator, Architectural Trades supports the planning, procurement, coordination, installation, inspection, and closeout of architectural construction packages for station and associated building areas. 
 Working closely with the Architectural Project Manager, site supervision, design consultants, quality teams, commercial teams, suppliers, and subcontractors, the Project Coordinator helps ensure that architectural work is executed safely, in the correct sequence, and in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, contract requirements, approved samples, applicable codes, and project quality standards. 
 The position focuses specifically on architectural and building-finish scopes, rather than civil works. These may include masonry, façade, drywall and partitions, ceilings, architectural metalwork, doors and hardware, glazing, roofing, waterproofing, cladding, flooring, tiling, painting, millwork, signage, louvers, firestopping, sealants, and other interior and exterior architectural finishes. 
 The salary range for this position is $90,000 CAD - $120,000 CAD, plus additional benefits.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Architectural Planning & Coordination 
 Coordinate architectural construction packages from design development and procurement through installation, inspection, deficiency correction, and final turnover.
 Review architectural drawings, reflected ceiling plans, room data sheets, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, method statements, and installation details. 
 Confirm that subcontractor shop drawings and technical submittals are coordinated with the latest approved design information before materials are released for fabrication or installation. 
 Identify discrepancies, missing information, constructability concerns, dimensional conflicts, and interface issues affecting architectural work. 
 Prepare, submit, track, and close Requests for Information relating to architectural design, finishes, materials, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, and installation requirements. 
 Coordinate architectural requirements with structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, communications, security, vertical transportation, and other interfacing disciplines. 
 Work with design and field teams to confirm wall openings, embeds, sleeves, access panels, equipment clearances, ceiling coordination, service penetrations, backing, supports, and finishing requirements. 
 Support the preparation of architectural work plans, look-ahead schedules, installation sequences, access requirements, logistics arrangements, and area-release plans. 
 Coordinate architectural samples, colour selections, material approvals, control samples, first-work inspections, and mock-ups. 
 Maintain architectural trackers for submittals, RFIs, samples, mock-ups, design changes, procurement, installation status, inspections, deficiencies, and closeout documentation. 
 Procurement, Construction, and Field Coordination 
 Assist in defining architectural subcontractor scopes of work and identifying scope gaps, exclusions, overlaps, and trade interfaces. 
 Support the preparation and review of bid packages, technical comparisons, scope clarifications, supplier proposals, subcontractor submissions, and procurement recommendations. 
 Coordinate with procurement teams, suppliers, fabricators, and architectural subcontractors to monitor material approvals, fabrication activities, delivery dates, storage requirements, and installation readiness. 
 Track long-lead architectural materials and equipment, including doors and hardware, glazing systems, cladding, specialty finishes, ceiling systems, architectural metalwork, millwork, signage, and custom-fabricated components. 
 Confirm that materials delivered to site correspond with approved submittals, samples, finishes, colours, quantities, and project requirements. 
 Monitor architectural activities in the field and coordinate with site supervisors and subcontractors to maintain the required work sequence and planned production. 
 Verify that work areas are ready before architectural subcontractors mobilize, including access, preceding-work completion, environmental conditions, dimensions, temporary services, material storage, and protection requirements. 
 Coordinate access, hoisting, work zones, laydown areas, temporary protection, material handling, and interfaces between architectural subcontractors operating in shared areas. 
 Participate in daily coordination meetings, weekly subcontractor meetings, look-ahead planning sessions, design reviews, quality meetings, and progress meetings. 
 Monitor architectural subcontractor manpower, productivity, work fronts, constraints, and scheduled completion dates. 
 Identify and escalate potential delays, incomplete prerequisites, design constraints, procurement risks, coordination conflicts, and quality concerns. 
 Support the development and implementation of practical mitigation and recovery measures. 
 Ensure architectural activities are carried out in compliance with project health and safety requirements, environmental requirements, approved work plans, and site procedures. 
 Quality, Compliance, and Closeout 
 Support quality assurance and quality control activities for architectural work. 
 Verify that architectural installations comply with approved drawings, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, manufacturer requirements, inspection and test plans, applicable codes, and project standards. 
 Coordinate inspections with subcontractors, site supervision, quality personnel, consultants, designers, authorities, and other stakeholders, as applicable. 
 Prepare and maintain inspection requests, checklists, deficiency lists, non-conformance records, corrective-action records, and associated quality documentation. 
 Monitor workmanship, alignment, tolerances, finishes, colour consistency, joint treatment, transitions, interfaces, protection, and final appearance. 
 Confirm that concealed architectural work and interfacing conditions are inspected before walls, ceilings, cladding systems, or other finishes are closed. 
 Coordinate testing and specialist inspections related to architectural systems, where required, including water penetration, adhesion, pull testing, sealant, firestopping, door operation, hardware functionality, and other specified performance requirements. 
 Manage architectural deficiencies from initial identification through correction, reinspection, acceptance, and closure. 
 Coordinate room-by-room, area-by-area, or system-based inspections and turnover activities. 
 Support the preparation of as-built drawings, warranties, maintenance information, attic stock records, spare-material inventories, operation and maintenance manuals, training records, product data, certificates, and turnover packages. 
 Confirm that architectural closeout documentation is complete, accurate, properly organized, and submitted in accordance with project requirements. 
 Support final cleaning, protection removal, touch-ups, finish repairs, and the presentation of completed areas for inspection and handover. 
 Progress Reporting, Cost Control, and Change Management 
 Track architectural progress by trade, area, level, work package, or construction zone. 
 Maintain accurate records of completed quantities, planned versus actual progress, outstanding work, constraints, deficiencies, and forecast completion dates. 
 Prepare weekly and monthly architectural progress reports, dashboards, photographs, trackers, and management updates. 
 Assist with schedule reviews and short-term planning for architectural packages, including three-week, six-week, and other project-specific look-ahead schedules. 
 Support quantity tracking, installed-progress measurement, subcontractor progress reviews, and payment-assessment processes. 
 Review subcontractor progress claims against actual work completed, accepted materials, approved changes, deficiencies, and supporting records. 
 Maintain records supporting architectural changes, including instructions, RFIs, site conditions, labour records, material records, photographs, quotations, and schedule impacts. 
 Assist in identifying potential changes, scope growth, rework, design development, and out-of-sequence work. 
 Support the review of subcontractor quotations and change-order documentation for completeness and alignment with the defined architectural scope. 
 Assist with cost forecasting, commitment tracking, accruals, quantity reconciliation, and architectural package cost reporting. 
 Monitor material waste, rework, damage, productivity, and subcontractor performance, and support corrective measures where needed. 
 Maintain accurate daily and weekly records to support progress verification, commercial discussions, schedule analysis, and dispute avoidance. 
 Identify trends, recurring constraints, and opportunities to improve architectural coordination, procurement, installation, inspection, and turnover processes.
College diploma or bachelor's degree (preferred) in Architecture, Architectural Technology, Construction Management, Building Science, Engineering Technology, or another construction-related discipline.
 Two to three years of experience in project coordination, construction coordination, architectural construction, building finishes, or a related construction environment. 
 Experience reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, shop drawings, material submissions, samples, and finish schedules.

 Strong understanding of the coordination required between architectural installations and mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire-protection, security, communications, and structural systems.

 Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple architectural packages, priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders. 
 Strong attention to detail, particularly regarding finishes, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, approved materials, and documentation status. 
 Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
 Ability to communicate professionally with project managers, superintendents, subcontractors, architects, consultants, suppliers, quality personnel, and client representatives. 
 Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary project team while maintaining ownership of assigned actions. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify practical solutions to architectural coordination and field-installation issues.

ABOUT THE INTERNSHIP 
 Program dates: 10 weeks, beginning in June and concluding in August. Exact program dates will be finalized and shared at a later dates.
 Application process: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and internship offers may be extended before the application period closes.
PROGRAM OVERVIEW 
 Egon Zehnder’s summer internship provides hands-on exposure to executive search and leadership advisory in a collaborative professional-services environment.
 Interns join the program as generalists and support live client assignments across industries, functions, and leadership topics. Working alongside researchers and consultants, interns contribute to research and search execution while learning how teams understand companies, assess markets, identify leadership talent, and support clients through complex leadership decisions.
 The program combines project work with structured onboarding and training, cross-practice shadowing, and mentorship from both research and consulting colleagues. Interns will also complete a capstone project focused on producing a practical output that can be reused by the firm beyond the summer.
 Please note that we are specifically seeking current undergraduate students, expected to graduate in 2028. 
 WHAT YOU WILL DO 
 Interns contribute to research, analysis, and project execution under the guidance of the team. Client and candidate relationship ownership remains with Egon Zehnder professionals.
 Support live executive search assignments through company and industry research, market mapping, and candidate identification.
 Help build and refine target-company and candidate lists using firm resources and available research tools.
 Analyze and synthesize information to support search strategy, team discussions, and decision-making.
 Prepare draft internal and client materials, including research summaries, profiles, presentations, trackers, and related documentation.
 Participate in internal search-team discussions and observe selected consultant or client-related conversations when appropriate.
 Work across industries and practice areas, with consideration given to your interests where project needs allow.
 Build relationships with a research mentor, a consulting mentor, and colleagues across the firm.
 Complete structured onboarding and training related to executive search, firm tools, research, search execution, and professional development.
 Complete a capstone project that addresses a real business need and produces a practical, reusable output.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 Students from all academic backgrounds are encouraged to apply. We are looking for candidates who demonstrate:
 Intellectual curiosity and an interest in understanding companies, industries, people, and leadership.
 Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
 Clear written and verbal communication.
 Attention to detail and sound judgment when working with confidential information.
 The ability to manage multiple priorities and collaborate across different teams.
 Initiative, professionalism, and comfort working in an environment where every project may be different.
 A willingness to ask questions, seek feedback, and learn through both hands-on work and observation.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint is preferred.
ELIGIBILITY 
 We are primarily seeking current college juniors who will be entering their senior year after the internship.
 Minimum GPA: 3.3. 
 This is a paid internship. 
 Strong performers may be considered for future opportunities based on business needs and role availability. 
 Visit our website to learn more about Egon Zehnder: https://www.egonzehnder.com/ 
The compensation for this internship is $25/hour
 About Egon Zehnder 
 Egon Zehnder is the world’s preeminent leadership advisory firm, inspiring leaders to navigate complex questions with human answers. We help organizations get to the heart of their leadership challenges and offer honest feedback and insights to help leaders realize their true being and purpose.
 We are built on a foundation that supports partnership in the truest sense of the word and aligns our interests with the interests of our clients. Our 560 consultants across 64 offices and 36 countries are former industry and functional leaders who collaborate seamlessly across geographies, industries and functions to deliver the full power of the Firm to every client, every time.
 We partner closely with public and private corporations, family-owned enterprises, and non-profit and government agencies to provide executive search, leadership solutions, CEO search and succession, and board advisory.
 We believe that together we can transform people, organizations and the world through leadership.
 Due to high volume, we will only be contacting applicants who meet all of the minimum requirements listed in the job description. Only those applicants who align most closely with our minimum and preferred qualifications will be contacted for an interview. The Recruiting team at Egon Zehnder will retain your application materials and may contact you regarding future opportunities. 
 ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 
 À PROPOS DU STAGE

 Processus de candidature : Les candidatures seront examinées au fur et à mesure, et des offres de stage pourront être proposées avant la fin de la période de candidature.
 APERÇU DU PROGRAMME 
 Le stage d’été d’Egon Zehnder offre une expérience pratique dans le domaine de la recherche de cadres supérieurs et du conseil en leadership, au sein d’un environnement de services professionnels axé sur la collaboration.
 Les stagiaires intègrent le programme en tant que généralistes et apportent leur soutien à des mandats clients concrets, couvrant divers secteurs d’activité, fonctions et enjeux liés au leadership. En travaillant aux côtés de chercheurs et de consultants, les stagiaires contribuent à la recherche et à la mise en œuvre des mandats, tout en apprenant comment les équipes analysent les entreprises, évaluent les marchés, identifient les talents de direction et accompagnent les clients dans leurs décisions complexes en matière de leadership.
 Le programme combine le travail sur des projets à une intégration et une formation structurées, à l’observation croisée entre les différents domaines d’expertise et au mentorat assuré par des collègues des équipes de recherche et de consultation. Les stagiaires réaliseront également un projet de fin de stage axé sur la production d’un résultat concret pouvant être réutilisé par l’entreprise au-delà de l’été.

 VOS MISSIONS 
 Les stagiaires contribuent à la recherche, à l’analyse et à la mise en œuvre des projets sous la supervision de l’équipe. La gestion des relations avec les clients et les candidats reste du ressort des professionnels d’Egon Zehnder.
 Appuyer les mandats de recherche de cadres en cours par le biais de recherches sur les entreprises et les secteurs d’activité, de l’analyse du marché et de l’identification de candidats.
 Contribuer à l’élaboration et au peaufinage des listes d’entreprises cibles et de candidats à l’aide des ressources du cabinet et des outils de recherche disponibles.
 Analyser et synthétiser les informations afin d’étayer la stratégie de recherche, les discussions d’équipe et la prise de décision.

 Participer aux discussions internes de l’équipe de recherche et assister, le cas échéant, à certaines conversations avec des consultants ou des clients.
 Travailler dans divers secteurs d’activité et domaines d’expertise, en tenant compte de vos intérêts lorsque les besoins des projets le permettent.
 Établir des relations avec un mentor en recherche, un mentor en consultation et des collègues de l’ensemble du cabinet.
 Suivre un programme d’intégration et de formation structuré portant sur la recherche de cadres supérieurs, les outils du cabinet, la recherche, la mise en œuvre des missions de recherche et le perfectionnement professionnel.
 Réaliser un projet de fin de formation qui répond à un besoin d’affaires réel et produit un résultat concret et réutilisable.
 CE QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS

 De curiosité intellectuelle et d’un intérêt pour la compréhension des entreprises, des secteurs d’activité, des personnes et du leadership.
 De solides compétences en recherche, en analyse et en résolution de problèmes.
 Une communication écrite et verbale claire.
 Le souci du détail et un bon jugement lors du traitement d’information confidentielle.
 La capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de collaborer avec différentes équipes.
 De l’initiative, du professionnalisme et l’aisance à travailler dans un environnement où chaque projet peut être différent.
 Une volonté de poser des questions, de solliciter des commentaires et d’apprendre tant par la pratique que par l’observation.
 La maîtrise de Microsoft Word, Excel et PowerPoint est un atout.
 ADMISSIBILITÉ
 Nous recherchons principalement des étudiants actuellement en troisième année d’université qui entreront en dernière année après le stage.
 Moyenne cumulative minimale : 3,3.
 Il s’agit d’un stage rémunéré.
 Les stagiaires les plus performants pourraient être pris en considération pour de futures occasions, selon les besoins de l’entreprise et les postes disponibles.
 Visitez notre site Web pour en savoir plus sur Egon Zehnder : https://www.egonzehnder.com/ 
 La rémunération pour ce stage est de 25 $ l'heure.
 À propos d’Egon Zehnder 
 Egon Zehnder est le cabinet de conseil en leadership le plus réputé au monde, qui inspire les dirigeants à relever des défis complexes en apportant des réponses humaines. Nous aidons les organisations à aller au cœur de leurs défis en matière de leadership et leur offrons des commentaires et des perspectives sincères afin d’aider les dirigeants à prendre conscience de leur véritable nature et de leur raison d’être.
 Notre structure repose sur des principes qui favorisent un partenariat au sens le plus authentique du terme et alignent nos intérêts sur ceux de nos clients. Nos 560 consultants, répartis dans 64 bureaux et 36 pays, sont d’anciens dirigeants sectoriels et fonctionnels qui collaborent de manière harmonieuse au-delà des frontières géographiques, des secteurs d’activité et des fonctions afin de mettre toute la puissance de notre cabinet au service de chaque client, à chaque fois.
 Nous travaillons en étroite collaboration avec des sociétés publiques et privées, des entreprises familiales, ainsi que des organismes sans but lucratif et des organismes gouvernementaux pour offrir des services de recherche de cadres supérieurs, des solutions de leadership, la recherche de PDG et la planification de la relève, ainsi que des conseils aux conseils d’administration.
 Nous croyons qu’ensemble, nous pouvons transformer les personnes, les organisations et le monde grâce au leadership.
 En raison du volume élevé de candidatures, nous ne communiquerons qu’avec les candidats qui répondent à toutes les exigences minimales énoncées dans la description de poste. Seuls les candidats dont le profil correspond le mieux à nos qualifications minimales et souhaitées seront invités à une entrevue. L’équipe de recrutement d’Egon Zehnder conservera votre dossier de candidature et pourrait communiquer avec vous au sujet d’occasions futures.

DO YOU LOVE KEEPING PEOPLE, OFFICES, AND GEAR RUNNING SMOOTHLY?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Manager, IT Operations to be part of our Operations department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn't like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That's why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The Team:

The IT team is one of the most cross-functional teams at Jobber. We build the systems, offices, and processes that scale as we transform our industry.

Our mission is to support our entire team through technology and first-class customer service. We keep our systems ahead of the curve and are always finding better ways for Jobberinos to do their best work. That includes you: through dedicated feedback, regular 1:1s, and endless learning opportunities, we want to accelerate your career too!

The Role:

Reporting to the Director, IT & Operations, the Manager, IT Operations will lead the IT Coordinator team, the people every Jobberino turns to when a laptop won't boot, a meeting room won't connect, or a new hire needs to be ready on day one. You're a player/coach: close enough to the work to spot what's slow or broken, and experienced enough to fix the process instead of just the ticket.

We're growing fast, and we don't want our support team to grow at the same rate. Your mandate is to deliver a better experience to more Jobberinos without a matching increase in headcount. That means fixing root causes, making self-serve genuinely good, and putting automation and AI to work on repeatable tasks, so your team spends its time where a human matters most.

This role is based in our Edmonton or Vancouver office, 4 days a week, with about 10% travel to our other offices. Our offices are where much of this work happens: meeting rooms, new-hire setups, company-wide standup, and a steady flow of hardware coming in and going out. You'll be the person on the ground who makes sure it all just works, for Jobberinos in Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, and everywhere in between.

Your team owns three things: office and workplace experience, the help desk, and the hardware lifecycle. You make sure all three run well at the same time.

The Manager, IT Operations will:

 - Partner with the Employee Experience team to keep our offices running well, from meeting rooms and AV to new-hire onboarding days.

 - Own the technical side of company-wide standup and all-hands, so they run smoothly no matter which office is hosting or where people are joining from.

 - Coordinate with facilities, vendors, and building management on the IT side of office moves, expansions, and changes.

 - Lead the IT Coordinators who work the queue, as their point of escalation, coach, and the person who removes what's slowing them down.

 - Own the health of the help desk, including response and resolution times, ticket volume and trends, and the quality of the support experience.

 - Turn repeat tickets into fixes by finding the root cause and choosing the right remedy: a process change, a knowledge article, a self-serve flow, or an AI automation built with IT Engineering. Then measure whether it worked.

 - Treat the knowledge base as a product, since it's what both people and AI answer from.

 - Own the performance of our AI-assisted support channels: what they handle, how well, and when they hand off to a human.

 - Set and report on the service levels that matter, and use the data to decide where the team spends its time.

Logistics Coordinator 
 Department: Supply Chain / Operations 
 Reports To: Planning & Logistics Manager
 Location: Ottawa (on-site)
 Employment Type: Full-Time
 Description 
 March Networks is an established global leader in the video surveillance industry and works with the world’s largest retailers and banking institutions. Our goal is to create a positive working environment where all of our employees can thrive. When you join our team, you’ll enjoy flexibility and support for a healthy work-life balance, as well as the professional development opportunities needed to advance your career. At March Networks, we value your hard work, creativity and your passionate desire to deliver only the best to our customers, partners and each other.
 Position Summary 
 Working with our third Party Order Fulfillment partners, the Logistics Coordinator handles the daily movement of goods in both directions. Outbound, that means finished products, components and demo equipment. Inbound and repair, which means customer returns, RMAs and repair orders. Where required, the role does the shipping, receiving, customs and carrier work to get shipments delivered on time, compliantly and at a reasonable cost, and works closely with carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, 3PLs and subcontracted repair centers.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Transportation & Shipping 
 Book domestic and international shipments by air, ocean, ground and courier. Pick the mode and carrier based on cost, transit time and service level.
 Act as the day-to-day contact for carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, 3PLs and repair service providers. Provide them with shipment instructions and direction.
 Track shipments and handle exceptions such as customs holds, delays, damaged goods and carrier issues. Update internal teams and customers on status.
 Give Sales, Customer Service and Professional Services shipment visibility and delivery estimates, and support field requirements.
 Customs & Trade Compliance 
 Prepare and manage customs paperwork, including commercial invoices, certificates of origin, HS/tariff classifications, and import/export licenses.
 Run denied party screening and applied export control classifications (ECCN, and ITAR where it applies) and country-specific import restrictions.
 Coordinate customs clearance for international returns and repair shipments, both outbound to repair centers and back to customers.
 Manage our duty accounts around the world to ensure where possible duty exposure is minimized and duty recovery is managed.
 Familiarity with CBP, ACE Portal and CARM Portal
 Reverse Logistics & Repair Orders 
 Process customer RMAs and internal and external repair orders, and make sure they are complete, documented and shipped on time.
 Coordinate shipments to and from subcontracted repair centers, following OEM repair instructions and processes.
 Inventory & Records 
 Check inventory levels and make stock transfers between warehouses and distribution hubs as needed.
 Keep shipment, repair and inventory transaction records accurate in the ERP/TMS.
 Transact inventory receipt and shipments from suppliers and to customers into and out of the March Networks ERP system (SAP)
 Qualifications 
 A diploma or degree in Supply Chain, Materials Management, International Trade or a related field, or equivalent experience.
 3+ years in logistics, shipping/receiving, customs or reverse logistics, ideally in a technology, electronics or manufacturing company.
 2+ years of inventory control experience.
 Working knowledge of Incoterms, customs procedures and export control requirements.
 Experience with freight forwarders, customs brokers and carriers across North America, EMEA and/or APAC.
 Comfortable with ERP and transportation systems (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite or similar, ACE Portal and CARM Portal) and with Excel.
 Strong customer service focus, organization and follow-through. Able to juggle many shipments against tight deadlines.
 Clear written and verbal communication with internal and external contacts, across time zones.
 Preferred certifications (asset, not required): CCS, CITP or an equivalent customs or trade certification.
 Work Environment 
 Mainly office-based, with regular time in the shipping and receiving area. The role involves using cargo knives, tape dispensers, pallet trucks and hand carts, and some physical effort.
 Requires focused attention and occasionally extra hours to meet shipping deadlines. There will be some early or late calls with overseas partners and carriers.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

About the role

We are looking for a versatile corporate and regulatory lawyer to join Cohere’s Legal team. Reporting to our Senior Governance Counsel, this role will support a global portfolio of corporate governance, entity and intercompany matters, together with cross-border regulatory, trade and compliance workstreams.



This role is designed for a lawyer with a strong corporate foundation who has also developed meaningful regulatory and trade experience. You should be comfortable moving between different types of legal work including:

 - supporting global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, intercompany arrangements and delegated authorities;

 - supporting cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment and national-security reviews, regulatory diligence and filing coordination;

 - helping the business navigate export-control, sanctions and related compliance requirements; and

 - supporting legal and regulatory issues arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements come into play.
   
   

You will work closely with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams, as well as with specialist external counsel in multiple jurisdictions. The role requires sound judgment, curiosity and the ability to take ownership of a workstream, identify when specialist advice is needed, and turn that advice into practical action.



What you’ll do

 - Support Cohere’s global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, board and shareholder matters, corporate approvals, delegated authorities, signing frameworks and ongoing entity maintenance.

 - Support Cohere’s intercompany legal architecture, including intercompany agreements and other cross-border operating arrangements, working closely with Finance, Tax, People and local counsel to ensure Cohere’s entities are structured and operated appropriately across jurisdictions.

 - Support cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, regulatory diligence, filing coordination and the implementation of regulatory commitments arising in connection with acquisitions, investments, restructurings and other significant matters.

 - Support Cohere’s export-control, sanctions and related compliance matters, including coordinating specialist external advice and translating regulatory requirements into practical internal guidance, controls and documentation.

 - Support legal and regulatory workstreams arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements need to be understood and operationalised.

 - Coordinate internal stakeholders and external counsel across jurisdictions, ensuring that legal and regulatory workstreams are appropriately scoped, progressed and implemented.

 - Take ownership of matters within the role’s remit and help develop practical, scalable approaches as Cohere’s international footprint grows.



What we’re looking for

 - A qualified lawyer with approximately 4–8 years of relevant experience, gained at a leading law firm, a sophisticated in-house legal team, or preferably a combination of both.

 - A strong corporate and cross-border legal foundation, with experience across areas such as subsidiary governance, entity structuring and reorganisations, intercompany arrangements, delegated authorities, corporate approvals and other aspects of international corporate practice.

 - Meaningful exposure to cross-border regulatory matters, particularly foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, export controls, sanctions, international trade or related corporate compliance issues. Deep specialism in any one of these areas is not required.

 - Experience working across multiple jurisdictions, including coordinating local and specialist external counsel and bringing different legal, regulatory and business inputs together into a coherent internal position.

 - Strong judgment, range and commercial awareness, with the ability to get quickly up to speed on unfamiliar issues, identify what matters most and distinguish issues that can be handled internally from those requiring specialist advice.

 - The ability to take ownership of an internal legal workstream, ask the right questions of specialist counsel, digest complex advice and translate it into clear, practical next steps for the business.

 - Clear and practical communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams.

 - A collaborative and pragmatic approach, with comfort moving between different subject areas and working across functions, jurisdictions and time zones.

 - Experience in technology, AI or another regulated industry would be helpful, but is not essential.

 - Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters is a plus but is not a prerequisite.



Nice to have

 - Experience in technology, AI, cloud or infrastructure, or another regulated industry.

 - Experience supporting a multinational organisation with a growing international entity footprint, particularly where legal, tax, finance and operational considerations intersect.

 - Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters, including procurement, digital sovereignty, security, accreditation or related market-access requirements.

 - Familiarity with North American, UK or EU regulatory frameworks relevant to cross-border technology businesses.
   
   

What success looks like

 - You can move comfortably between corporate and regulatory matters, identify the core issue quickly and make progress even where the work does not fit neatly into a single legal category.

 - You can take ownership of a complex cross-border workstream, bring together the right internal stakeholders and external advisers, and drive it through to a practical outcome.

 - You know when specialist advice is needed, can frame the right questions for external counsel, and can turn complex advice into clear, actionable guidance for the business.

 - You become a trusted execution partner across Cohere’s corporate governance and regulatory portfolio, taking meaningful ownership of workstreams and creating capacity for more strategic, cross-functional and government-facing work at the senior level.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.
